newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Union says Russian 1997 gold output down to 80 T.
newsitem.headline: Union says Russian 1997 gold output down to 80 T.

text.p: Russia will produce 80 tonnes of gold in 1997, down from 100 tonnes in 1996, due to falling prices on world markets, Interfax news agency quoted a mining union official as saying on Tuesday.

It quoted Irina Ledenyova, deputy chairwoman of the Russian Mining and Metallurgists Union, as providing the figures. Different Russian officials have quoted different figures for 1997 and 1996 gold output.
Other officials see Russia's 1997 gold output in the range of 95-110 tonnes, down from approximately 124 tonnes in 1996.
Miners say output in Russia, the world's fifth largest gold producer with the world's third largest reserves in the ground, will fall if the state does not provide more funds.
